passages.text: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed from the entrance.
passages.sermon:
Mary Magdalene was a follower of Jesus.
She went to the tomb early on the first day of the week.
It was still dark outside.
She arrived at the tomb.
She saw that someone had removed the stone from the entrance.
passages.original: Τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ἔρχεται πρωῒ σκοτίας ἔτι οὔσης εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ βλέπει τὸν λίθον ἠρμένον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου

passages.text: So she came running to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved. “They have taken the Lord out of the tomb,” she said, “and we do not know where they have put Him!”
passages.sermon:
Mary Magdalene saw the stone was removed from the tomb.
She ran quickly.
She went to Simon Peter.
She also went to the other disciple.
Jesus loved this other disciple.
Mary spoke to them.
She said, “They have taken the Lord out of the tomb.”
She also said, “We do not know where they have put Him.”
passages.original: τρέχει οὖν καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς Σίμωνα Πέτρον καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἄλλον μαθητὴν ὃν ἐφίλει ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἦραν τὸν Κύριον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου καὶ οὐκ οἴδαμεν ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν

passages.text: Then Peter and the other disciple set out for the tomb.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Another disciple was with Peter.
Peter and the other disciple left.
They went to the tomb.
passages.original: Ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Πέτρος καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητής καὶ ἤρχοντο εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον

passages.text: The two were running together, but the other disciple outran Peter and reached the tomb first.
passages.sermon: Peter and the other disciple ran together to the tomb.\r\nThe other disciple ran faster than Peter.\r\nThe other disciple reached the tomb first.
passages.original: ἔτρεχον δὲ οἱ δύο ὁμοῦ καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς προέδραμεν τάχιον τοῦ Πέτρου καὶ ἦλθεν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον

passages.text: He bent down and looked in at the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.
passages.sermon:
The other disciple arrived at the tomb first.
He bent down at the entrance.
He looked inside the tomb.
He saw the linen cloths lying there.
He did not go into the tomb.
passages.original: καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει κείμενα τὰ ὀθόνια οὐ μέντοι εἰσῆλθεν

passages.text: Simon Peter arrived just after him. He entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there.
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Simon Peter followed the other disciple to the tomb.
Simon Peter arrived just after the other disciple.
Simon Peter entered the tomb.
Simon Peter saw the linen cloths lying there.
passages.original: Ἔρχεται οὖν καὶ Σίμων Πέτρος ἀκολουθῶν αὐτῷ καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ θεωρεῖ τὰ ὀθόνια κείμενα

passages.text: The cloth that had been around Jesus’ head was rolled up, lying separate from the linen cloths.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had a cloth around his head.
This cloth was not with the linen cloths.
Someone had rolled up the head cloth.
The head cloth was lying in a separate place.
passages.original: καὶ τὸ σουδάριον ὃ ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ οὐ μετὰ τῶν ὀθονίων κείμενον ἀλλὰ χωρὶς ἐντετυλιγμένον εἰς ἕνα τόπον

passages.text: Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in. And he saw and believed.
passages.sermon:
The other disciple arrived at the tomb first.
This disciple was not Simon Peter.
He also entered the tomb.
He saw what was inside the tomb.
He believed.
passages.original: τότε οὖν εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς ὁ ἐλθὼν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ εἶδεν καὶ ἐπίστευσεν

passages.text: For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.
passages.sermon:
The disciples did not understand the Scripture.
The Scripture said Jesus had to rise from the dead.
The disciples did not know this yet.
They did not realize Jesus must rise from the dead.
passages.original: οὐδέπω γὰρ ᾔδεισαν τὴν γραφὴν ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι

passages.text: Then the disciples returned to their homes.
passages.sermon: The disciples were followers of Jesus.\r\nThe disciples left the tomb.\r\nThe disciples went back to their homes.
passages.original: Ἀπῆλθον οὖν πάλιν πρὸς αὑτοὺς οἱ μαθηταί

passages.text: But Mary stood outside the tomb weeping. And as she wept, she bent down to look into the tomb, and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet.
passages.sermon:
Mary stood outside the tomb.
She was weeping.
As Mary wept, she bent down to look into the tomb.
She saw two angels.
The angels wore white.
The angels were sitting where the body of Jesus had been.
One angel sat at the head.
The other angel sat at the feet.
passages.original: Μαρία δὲ εἱστήκει πρὸς τῷ μνημείῳ ἔξω κλαίουσα ὡς οὖν ἔκλαιεν παρέκυψεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ θεωρεῖ δύο ἀγγέλους ἐν λευκοῖς καθεζομένους ἕνα πρὸς τῇ κεφαλῇ καὶ ἕνα πρὸς τοῖς ποσίν ὅπου ἔκειτο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: “Woman, why are you weeping?” they asked. “Because they have taken my Lord away,” she said, “and I do not know where they have put Him.”
passages.sermon:
Two angels sat inside the tomb.
They wore white clothes.
They spoke to Mary.
They said, “Woman, why are you weeping?”
Mary answered them.
She said, “They have taken my Lord away.”
She said, “I do not know where they have put Him.”
passages.original: Καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῇ ἐκεῖνοι Γύναι τί κλαίεις Λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὅτι Ἦραν τὸν Κύριόν μου καὶ οὐκ οἶδα ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν

passages.text: When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there; but she did not recognize that it was Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Mary spoke to the angels.
She turned around.
She saw a man standing there.
This man was Jesus.
Mary did not know it was Jesus.
passages.original: Ταῦτα εἰποῦσα ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἑστῶτα καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν

passages.text: “Woman, why are you weeping?” Jesus asked. “Whom are you seeking?” Thinking He was the gardener, she said, “Sir, if you have carried Him off, tell me where you have put Him, and I will get Him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman.
Jesus said, “Woman, why are you weeping?”
Jesus said, “Whom are you seeking?”
The woman thought Jesus was the gardener.
She said to Him, “Sir, if you have carried Him away, tell me where you have put Him.”
She said, “I will get Him.”
passages.original: λέγει αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς Γύναι τί κλαίεις τίνα ζητεῖς Ἐκείνη δοκοῦσα ὅτι ὁ κηπουρός ἐστιν λέγει αὐτῷ Κύριε εἰ σὺ ἐβάστασας αὐτόν εἰπέ μοι ποῦ ἔθηκας αὐτόν κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἀρῶ

passages.text: Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said to Him in Hebrew, “Rabboni!” (which means “Teacher”).
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood near Mary Magdalene.
Jesus spoke to her.
Jesus said, “Mary.”
Mary heard Jesus say her name.
Mary turned toward Jesus.
Mary spoke to Jesus in Hebrew.
Mary said, “Rabboni!”
“Rabboni” means “Teacher.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς Μαριάμ Στραφεῖσα ἐκείνη λέγει αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστί Ραββουνι ὃ λέγεται Διδάσκαλε

passages.text: “Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Mary Magdalene.
He said, “Do not cling to Me.”
He said, “I have not yet ascended to the Father.”
He said, “Go to My brothers.”
He said, “Tell them this.”
He said, “I am ascending to My Father.”
He said, “He is your Father also.”
He said, “I am ascending to My God.”
He said, “He is your God also.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς Μή μου ἅπτου οὔπω γὰρ ἀναβέβηκα πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα πορεύου δὲ πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφούς μου καὶ εἰπὲ αὐτοῖς Ἀναβαίνω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα μου καὶ Πατέρα ὑμῶν καὶ Θεόν μου καὶ Θεὸν ὑμῶν

passages.text: Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord!” And she told them what He had said to her.
passages.sermon:
Mary Magdalene was a follower of Jesus.
She went to the disciples.
She announced to them, “I have seen the Lord!”
She told the disciples what Jesus had said to her.
passages.original: Ἔρχεται Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ἀγγέλλουσα τοῖς μαθηταῖς ὅτι Ἑώρακα τὸν Κύριον καὶ ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῇ

passages.text: It was the first day of the week, and that very evening, while the disciples were together with the doors locked for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them. “Peace be with you!” He said to them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the risen Lord.
It was evening on the first day of the week.
The disciples were together in one place.
They had locked the doors.
They were afraid of the Jews.
Jesus came to them.
He stood among them.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Peace be with you!”
passages.original: Οὔσης οὖν ὀψίας τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ τῇ μιᾷ σαββάτων καὶ τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων ὅπου ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν

passages.text: After He had said this, He showed them His hands and His side. The disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had just spoken to His disciples.
He showed them His hands.
He showed them His side.
The disciples saw the Lord.
The disciples rejoiced.
passages.original: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἔδειξεν καὶ τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τὴν πλευρὰν αὐτοῖς Ἐχάρησαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες τὸν Κύριον

passages.text: Again Jesus said to them, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples again.
He said, “Peace be with you.”
The Father sent Me.
Now I am sending you.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν καθὼς ἀπέσταλκέν με ὁ Πατήρ κἀγὼ πέμπω ὑμᾶς

passages.text: When He had said this, He breathed on them and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He finished speaking.
He breathed on them.
He said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit.”
passages.original: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἐνεφύσησεν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Λάβετε Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον

passages.text: If you forgive anyone his sins, they are forgiven; if you withhold forgiveness from anyone, it is withheld.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus had just given them the Holy Spirit.
Jesus said, “If you forgive anyone’s sins, those sins are forgiven.”
Jesus also said, “If you do not forgive anyone’s sins, those sins are not forgiven.”
passages.original: ἄν τινων ἀφῆτε τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἀφέωνται αὐτοῖς ἄν τινων κρατῆτε κεκράτηνται

passages.text: Now Thomas called Didymus, one of the Twelve, was not with the disciples when Jesus came.
passages.sermon: Thomas was one of the Twelve disciples.\r\nPeople also called him Didymus.\r\nThomas was not with the other disciples when Jesus came.
passages.original: Θωμᾶς δὲ εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος οὐκ ἦν μετ’ αὐτῶν ὅτε ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: So the other disciples told him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he replied, “Unless I see the nail marks in His hands, and put my finger where the nails have been, and put my hand into His side, I will never believe.”
passages.sermon:
Thomas was one of the Twelve disciples.
People also called him Didymus.
Thomas was not with the other disciples when Jesus came.
The other disciples spoke to Thomas.
They said, “We have seen the Lord.”
Thomas answered them.
He said, “I must see the nail marks in Jesus’ hands.”
He said, “I must put my finger where the nails were.”
He said, “I must put my hand into Jesus’ side.”
He said, “If I do not do these things, I will not believe.”
passages.original: ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ οἱ ἄλλοι μαθηταί Ἑωράκαμεν τὸν Κύριον Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐὰν μὴ ἴδω ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτοῦ τὸν τύπον τῶν ἥλων καὶ βάλω τὸν δάκτυλόν μου εἰς τὸν τύπον τῶν ἥλων καὶ βάλω μου τὴν χεῖρα εἰς τὴν πλευρὰν αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ πιστεύσω

passages.text: Eight days later, His disciples were once again inside with the doors locked, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus had twelve main disciples.
Thomas was one of these twelve disciples.
Eight days after Jesus first appeared, the disciples gathered inside a house.
They locked the doors.
Thomas was with the disciples this time.
Jesus came to them.
He stood among the disciples.
Jesus said, “Peace be with you.”
passages.original: Καὶ μεθ’ ἡμέρας ὀκτὼ πάλιν ἦσαν ἔσω οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ Θωμᾶς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔρχεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον καὶ εἶπεν Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν

passages.text: Then Jesus said to Thomas, “Put your finger here and look at My hands. Reach out your hand and put it into My side. Stop doubting and believe.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Thomas.
Jesus said, “Put your finger here.
Look at My hands.
Reach out your hand.
Put your hand into My side.
Do not doubt.
Believe.”
passages.original: εἶτα λέγει τῷ Θωμᾷ Φέρε τὸν δάκτυλόν σου ὧδε καὶ ἴδε τὰς χεῖράς μου καὶ φέρε τὴν χεῖρά σου καὶ βάλε εἰς τὴν πλευράν μου καὶ μὴ γίνου ἄπιστος ἀλλὰ πιστός

passages.text: Thomas replied, “My Lord and my God!”
passages.sermon:
Thomas was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Thomas saw Jesus standing among the disciples.
Thomas spoke to Jesus.
Thomas said, “My Lord and my God!”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Θωμᾶς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὁ Κύριός μου καὶ ὁ Θεός μου

passages.text: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen Me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Thomas.
Jesus said, “You have seen Me.
You have believed because you saw Me.
Blessed are those who have not seen Me.
They have believed without seeing.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὅτι ἑώρακάς με πεπίστευκας μακάριοι οἱ μὴ ἰδόντες καὶ πιστεύσαντες

passages.text: Jesus performed many other signs in the presence of His disciples, which are not written in this book.
passages.sermon:
Jesus performed many other signs.
He did these signs in the presence of His disciples.
These signs are not written in this book.
passages.original: Πολλὰ μὲν οὖν καὶ ἄλλα σημεῖα ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐνώπιον τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν γεγραμμένα ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ

passages.text: But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name.
passages.sermon:
These words are written here.
They are written for a purpose.
The purpose is that you may believe Jesus is the Christ.
Jesus is the Son of God.
If you believe in Jesus, you will have life.
You will have life through His name.
passages.original: ταῦτα δὲ γέγραπται ἵνα πιστεύητε ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἵνα πιστεύοντες ζωὴν ἔχητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ
